weather_report:
McMahons Point wakes under a clear, rinsed-blue sky, the harbour glassy and a little shy in the early light. The air is crisp enough to make breath feel honest, yet the sun already has that winter-bright resolve that sharpens edges and sends shadows walking. Skies are set to stay clean and bright through late morning into early afternoon, the day looking beautifully transparent with long, unbroken views. With the sun so unfiltered, the UV will lift from gentle to insistent by midday; it may be winter, but your skin will still notice.

Expect a day that moves from brisk to comfortably mild. Dress in light layers you can peel back, with sunglasses, a hat, and a touch of sunscreen for the peak hours. It’s a fine morning for small, satisfying errands on foot, a lingered coffee on a sunny bench, or hanging the washing where it can drink the light. Around lunch, a quiet amble along the foreshore or a ferry ride taken on the windward side will feel just right—simple pleasures made clearer by the kind of sky that doesn’t try to complicate things.
